newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Prodi sees budget clinching Italian Euro entry.
newsitem.headline: Prodi sees budget clinching Italian Euro entry.

text.p: The 1997 budget will be sufficient for Italy to join a planned single European currency, Italian Prime Minister Ramano Prodi said on Tuesday.
Prodi said talks between his centre-left administration and other parties were continuing, but he was confident of getting approval of the budget, expected to be presented on Friday.
Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi plans to introduce a tough package, including cuts in health and pensions spending, to prepare Italy for the launch of the single currency in 1999.
But these plans have faced opposition from key government supporter, the hard-left Communist Refoundation.
"The budget will be sufficient to bring Italy into Europe," Prodi told reporters on the final day of a two-day visit to the Netherlands.
He also repeated his previous view that there was no room for Italy to delay entry into the planned Euro currency beyond the initial date of 1999.
He said European countries not among the initial entry group would be "horribly damaged".
"I will not be the prime minister who leaves Italy out of the European Union. Not only Italy needs Europe, but Europe needs Italy," Prodi added.
Italy needs a tough budget because it currently does not meet any of the criteria specified by the Maastrict Treaty for countries wishing to sign up for the single currency.
